State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
State Bank Of India vs Md. Subhan on 24 September, 2015
Cause Title/Judgement-Entry STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION WEST BENGAL 11A, Mirza Ghalib Street, Kolkata - 700087   First Appeal No. FA/540/2014 (Arisen out of Order Dated 08/04/2014 in Case No. CC/320/2012 of District Kolkata-II)   1. State Bank of India Local Head Office, Samridhhi Bhawan, 1, Strand Road, P.S. Hare Street, Kolkata-700 001. 2. The Branch Manager, representing State Bank of India Kidderpore Dock Yard Area Branch, Garden Reach Road, P.S.-W.P.P.S., Kolkata -700 024. ...........Appellant(s) Versus 1. Md. Subhan S/o Late Sk. Alam, G-58, Mirza House, Battikal(1st Lane), P.O. Matiabruz, Garden Reach, P.S. Metiabruz, Kolkata - 700 024. ...........Respondent(s)   BEFORE:     HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KALIDAS MUKHERJEE PRESIDENT   HON'BLE MR. TARAPADA GANGOPADHYAY MEMBER   HON'BLE MR. UTPAL KUMAR BHATTACHARYA MEMBER   For the Appellant: Mr. Surajit Auddy Mrs. Swapnalekha Auddy , Advocate For the Respondent: Inperson/, Advocate ORDER 24.09.2015

 MR. TARAPADA GANGOPADHYAY, HON'BLE MEMBER
The present Appeal
u/s 15
of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 has been filed challenging the judgment and order dated 8.4.2014 passed by the Ld. District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Kolkata, Unit-II, in C.C.No. 320 of 2012, directing the OPs to jointly and severally refund and pay within 45 days to the Complainant Rs. 35,000/- along with simple interest '@ 8%' since the date of 'fraudulent' withdrawal of the same till its full payment is made.  The OPs were also directed to pay within the said period Rs. 10,000/- as cost and Rs. 5,000/- as compensation, failing which interest @ 100/- per day for the entire period of default shall have to be deposited with the 'Forum' by the OPs.
Facts of the case, in brief, are that the Respondent/Complainant used to hold an ATM card bearing No. 6220180792000001703 against his S.B.A/c 10770780419 with the Khidirpur Dock Yard Area Branch  of the Appellants/OPs-Bank.  On 5.3.2012 at 15:07 hours when the Respondent/Complainant withdrew Rs. 5,000/- by the said ATM Card, his credit balance was shown as Rs. 6,53,001.90, and that such credit balance, when on 10.3.2012 the Respondent/ Complainant further withdrew Rs. 8,000/- by the said ATM Card, was shown as Rs. 6,10,001.90 instead of Rs. 6,45,000.90, thereby pointing to the false withdrawal of Rs. 35,000/- on 5.3.2012 immediately after the said undisputed withdrawal of Rs. 5,000/- by the Respondent/Complainant on 5.3.2012 as alleged.  Noticing such allegedly unauthorized withdrawal of money the Respondent/ Complainant lodged a complaint with the Appellants/OPs-Bank and also with the Banking Ombudsman, but without any success.  Then the Respondent/ Complainant filed the instant Complaint before the Ld. District Forum concerned alleging deficiency in service on the part of the Appellants/OPs-Bank for their failure to provide adequate safety and security of the money of the Respondent/ Complainant as also for their failure to provide video footage of the disputed transaction.  With this factual background, the Ld. District Forum passed the impugned judgment and order in the aforesaid manner.  Aggrieved by such order the OPs have preferred the instant Appeal.
The Ld. Advocate for the Appellants/OPs-Bank filing BNA submits that the Ld. District Forum failed to consider that because of the elaborate safety procedure as observed by the banking system, an unauthorized person cannot withdraw any money through ATM even if the unauthorized person is able to clone the ATM card of the actual ATM card-holder.
The Ld. Advocate further submits that no money can be withdrawn from ATM without coincidence of the ATM Card and the PIN, which remain under the exclusively personal and confidential custody of the ATM card-holder, and for access to which by any person other than the ATM card-holder himself, the ATM card-holder cannot shake off his own liability.
The Ld. Advocate also submits that non-supply of the CCTV footage has no relevance as because this is not the case of the Respondent/Complainant that he did not go to operate the ATM of the Appellants/OPs-Bank.
In support of the aforesaid submission the Ld. Advocate has relied upon a number of decisions of the Hon'ble National Commission, such as, (
1) State Bank of India Vs. K.K.Bhalla
, reported in 2011 (2) CPR 26 (NC), (2) State Bank of India Vs. Om Prakash Saini, decided on 18.1.2013 by the Hon'ble National Commission in
Revision Petition No. 2382 of 2012, (3) Raghabendra Nath Sen & Anr. Vs. Punjab National Bank
, decided on 17.12.2014 by the Hon'ble National Commission in
Revision Petition No. 3973 of 2014 and (4) State Bank of India Vs. Subhasis Chowdhury
, decided on 18.2.2015 by the Hon'ble National Commission in Revision Petition No. 545 of 2013, wherein the ratio was decided that in view of the elaborate procedure evolved by the Appellants/OPs-Bank to ensure safety of the money of the customer of the Bank, it is not possible for money to be withdrawn by any unauthorized person from ATM without the ATM Card and knowledge of PIN.
The Ld. Advocate finally submits that the Bank Statement, as available on records, exhibits the withdrawal of the amount in question, which the Respondent/Complainant could not counter by support of any documentary evidence in his favour.
The Ld. Advocate concludes that in view of the aforesaid submissions and the decisions of the Hon'ble National Commission, the instant Appeal should be allowed and the impugned judgment and order be set aside.
On the other hand, the Respondent/Complainant, appearing in person, repelling the aforesaid statements by the Ld. Advocate for the Appellants/OPs-Bank, submits that the 'Customer Transactions' Statement, as available on records, shows that the disputed amount was withdrawn on 5.3.2012 at 15:09:31 hours from the ATM being ID No. S10B003084077, which was not operated by the Respondent/Complainant while he himself withdrew Rs. 5,000/- on 5.3.2012 at 15:07:24 hours, i.e. immediately before his own withdrawal of Rs. 5,000/- from the ATM being ID No. S10A0030876, which is different from the ATM ID from which the disputed amount was unauthorisedly withdrawn.
The Respondent/Complainant continues that the event of withdrawal of the disputed amount of Rs. 35,000/- from the separate ATM indicates the fraudulent withdrawal of the disputed amount.
The Respondent/Complainant also submits that the Appellants/OPs did not provide any video footage to identify the person who was involved in the withdrawal of the disputed amount from the ATM which is different from the ATM which he himself operated for withdrawal of Rs. 5,000/- a few minutes before withdrawal of the disputed amount.
The Respondent/Complainant adds that thus, the Appellants/OPs-Bank being the custodian of the money of the Respondent/Complainant-Customer, did not render adequate and qualitative service of security in respect of the money of the Respondent/Complainant-Customer and that such failure on the part of the Appellants/OPs-Bank constitutes deficiency in service on their part.
The Respondent/Complainant concludes that in view of the submission so put forward, the impugned judgment and order should be sustained.
We have heard both the sides, considered their respective submission and perused the materials on records.
'ATM Customer Advice' Sheet, as available on records, exhibits the withdrawal of the disputed amount of Rs. 35,000/- on 5.3.2012 (Running Page-21 of Memo of Appeal), which is also corroborated by the 'Customer Transactions' Statement, as available on records (Running Page-32 of Memo of Appeal).  Against the aforesaid documentary evidence the Respondent/Complainant has not been able to furnish any counter-evidence.
It is well-settled that in view of the elaborate security procedure generally adopted by the banks in case of operation of the ATM, it is not possible to withdraw any money from the ATM by any unauthorized person until and unless the ATM Card and the PIN thereof fall on wrong hand, for which none but the card-holder should be held liable because the ATM card and the PIN are held under the exclusively personal and confidential custody of the card-holder.  In this respect, we find strong force in the submission of the Ld. Advocate for the Appellants/OPs-Bank as also his reliance on the decisions of the Hon'ble National Commission as referred to hereinbefore.
In view of the evidence on records as well as of the decisions of the Hon'ble National Commission, as referred to hereinbefore, we have no option but to allow the Appeal and set aside the impugned judgment and order of the Ld. District Forum, which appears to have been passed against the settled principle of law in respect of the matter on hand.
In the result, the Appeal is allowed and the impugned judgment and order is set aside.  The Petition of Complaint is dismissed.  No order as to costs.      [HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KALIDAS MUKHERJEE] PRESIDENT
